title: Routing forensics: adaptive metrics bridge for per-request provenance
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build an 'adaptive metrics bridge' that attaches lightweight per-request provenance and rolling per-hop micro-metrics to routing decisions, while controlling cardinality and storage cost. This ticket scopes the engineering work to capture a searchable forensic trail for requests that can be sampled, rehydrated, and used by SRE/SEs and support for RCA/playback without overwhelming our telemetry backend.

Background: Current routing telemetry is inconsistent across region/tier fallbacks and model-variant substitutions. We lack a compact, queryable linkage between a request and the sequence of routing decisions (region chosen, tier chosen, variant fallback, latency per decision, policy reason). Existing artifacts capture lots of high-fidelity traces or very coarse logs; both have gaps for quick forensics.

Scope of this ticket (deliverables):
- Define a compact per-request provenance envelope (ProvenanceID, decision_sequence[], decision_summaries, cost_estimate, final_choice) encoded as a structured event designed for high-cardinality sampling.
- Implement adaptive sampling rules based on error-rate, latency anomalies, and customer tier; default sampling 0.5% with sticky escalation for correlated anomalies.
- Per-hop micro-metrics: capture three numeric fields per hop (decision_latency_ms, queue_delay_ms, token_cost_microunits) and one categorical field (policy_reason).
- Add an enrichment step to attach the envelope to existing request traces (trace_id link) and the response header for debug mode (+ short provenance token).
- Storage/retention: store sampled envelopes in a compressed time-series index for 14 days; aggregated rollups (per model/region/tier) retained 90 days.
- Query and playback: add a Light UI hook in Console -> Requests to fetch and replay the sampled decision stream (prototype endpoint only).

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change routing logic or fallback policies themselves.
- It does not implement full-text replay of model inputs (we will attach reference pointers only for PII safety).

Design notes / trade-offs considered:
- Compact schema vs. fidelity: We intentionally limit per-hop fields to fixed small vectors to control cardinality. Full decision dumps will remain available only for on-demand SOC captures.
- Sampling policy: Favor anomaly-driven sampling to increase signal when things go wrong while keeping steady-state cost low. This balances customer-impact visibility and telemetry expense.
- Storage backend: Use our existing trace-store S3-backed index with compressed msgpack blocks to avoid adding a new DB. Cost model shows ~12-18% increase in monthly telemetry spend at default sample rate.
- Privacy & security: We will not persist raw prompts. Envelopes may contain hashed request fingerprints and pointers to artifacts stored in a gated storage with KMS. Security review required.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Provenance envelope schema approved by Observability and Product teams and documented in Confluence (link in attachments).
2) Production-safe ingestion of sampled envelopes without noticeable tail-latency increase (<1ms median extra CPU on router path).
3) Adaptive sampling triggers correctly escalate sample rate during a simulated outage/workload spike test.
4) Console prototype can fetch and present a sampled decision stream for individual requests (pagination + download).
5) CI tests for envelope encoding/decoding and privacy redaction present.

Monitoring / Alerts:
- Alert if ingestion error rate for envelopes > 0.1% for five minutes.
- Cost alert if storage for envelope index growth > 20% of forecast in a rolling week.

Operational playbook (outline):
- How to enable debug-mode provenance header for a customer.
- Steps to pull a full decision stream and request a SOC export if higher fidelity is needed.

Implementation plan (phases):
A) Schema + sampling engine (2 weeks): define proto/JSON schema and server-side sampling rules.
B) Router instrumentation (3 weeks): attach envelope generation to routing layer and emit to trace-store via async producer.
C) Console prototype + APIs (2 weeks): implement fetch endpoints and minimal UI to view decision stream.
D) Hardening & rollout (2 weeks): load test, security review, and incremental enablement on canary region.
